_what: One brief per FORMAT: the shots that make a variation — same man, same layout, same words, same bar; only the picture changes. Instantiated per unit into ads/<slug>/variations.json.
portraitvoid: chin lifted, neck turned to camera, product held at the jaw
seated, three-quarter angle, product in the open palm
tight close-up on beard line and neck, product just entering frame
productvoid: product angled 30° in the raised hand, bristles toward camera
product held lower, palm open, dome facing up
the product set down on the basin edge, the man's neck behind it out of focus
twopanel: top panel: the neck from the other side; bottom: same fix, product held higher
top panel: the collar pulled down on the other side; bottom: the product flat against that same patch
top panel: chin lifted; bottom: bristles pressed flat against the skin, foam visible

the man leaning over the sink, one hand on the rim, product held at the jawline
the man with a towel round his shoulders at the basin, product just off the skin below the ear

the man leaning toward the mirror, free hand stretching the skin under his chin to see it
the man half-turned in the mirror to catch the side of his neck over his shoulder

the poster on the wall above the sink, the man leaning in close to the glass to see the bumps under his jaw
the man tugging his collar down in front of the poster, head turned to show the side of his neck

_rule: A VARIATION CHANGES THE MOMENT, INSIDE THE WORLD OF THE PROBLEM. Two ways to get this wrong and both have been made. (1) Change only the camera — 'harder light', 'tighter crop', 'slight angle', 'different card stock'. Those come back as the same picture: a hash over the first 110 found 16 renders indistinguishable from a sibling, every one from a camera-only brief. (2) Change the location out of the subject — the first rewrite sent Beto to a kitchen with a mug. Damon: 'this is slop'. He was right. The ad is about bumps on his neck; a man making coffee is a stock photo with a product dropped in. So: stay where the problem lives — the mirror, the sink, the collar, the lineup, the neck, the shirt going on — and move him within it. The briefs that always worked (captionbox, portraitvoid, twopanel) never left that world.
_test: Read the three lines. (a) Could two be the same photograph a second apart? Not finished. (b) Could a line be an ad for anything else — coffee, a kitchen, a nice morning? Not finished. It has to be a man with this problem, at the moment he notices it.
_never: Never describe anything that overlaps, peels, curls, tears or crops the layout itself. The poster IS the ad; a half-peeled corner ate the headline on 2026-09-11. Move the man, never the artwork.
